title: Compact resident-window coordinator and GPU swap mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a compact resident-window coordinator (RWC) for the paged/blocked KV cache to reduce GPU OOMs and reduce swap thrash under continuous batching workloads. The RWC replaces the coarse global residency heuristic with a lightweight moving window per-GPU that tracks token residency at block granularity and exposes stable pinning hints to the batch router and swap controller.

Goals:
- Reduce end-to-end latency variance during mixed-latency batches by avoiding mid-batch host swap of hot blocks.
- Keep steady-state resident set below configured GPU residency budgets while preserving quality by selectively keeping hot prefixes resident.
- Provide fast, constant-time residency decisions suitable for high QPS continuous batching.
- Integrate with existing host-swap path as graceful fallback and maintain safe concurrency with existing KV writes.

Key ideas / design:
1) Block layout and compact index:
- KV is already sharded into fixed-size blocks (default 256KB). Add a compact per-block residency index stored in GPU DRAM metadata region: a single 8-bit hotness counter + 8-bit age token + 1-bit pinned flag per block. This keeps metadata ~2 bytes per 256KB block (~0.0008% overhead).
- The RWC maintains a circular resident window: a contiguous logical range of block IDs designated as the candidate resident set for a given GPU. The window moves gradually based on observed serving patterns.

2) Hotness scoring and window movement:
- On each batch, kernel-level access traces increment the block hotness counters (saturating at 255). At epoch boundaries (~1s), we decay counters by right-shifting by 1 and update age tokens so we can prefer recently-accessed blocks.
- Window movement heuristic favors blocks with hotness above a tunable threshold OR blocks pinned by policy (see pinning). Move is limited to N blocks per epoch to avoid large churn.

3) Pinning policy and batch-affinity pins:
- Short-lived "batch-affinity" pins: when a request that is expected to generate multiple token requests in the same RPC (long chat turn / long prefix) touches a block, we temporarily pin the block for the duration of the active KV sequence (microseconds to milliseconds). This prevents mid-batch host swap.
- Long-lived pins: controlled by the RWC when a block repeatedly scores above the threshold across epochs. Long pins consume a portion of the residency budget and are limited by a global pinned quota.

4) Integration with continuous batching and router:
- Batch router exposes an API to RWC: before dispatching a merged batch, the router queries the RWC for an ordered list of blocks that will likely be needed. The RWC returns a small prioritized hint list (up to 64 block IDs) which the router uses to pre-attach KV slices or avoid work-stealing to GPUs missing these hot blocks.
- If prefetch into GPU memory is necessary, we do a lightweight async host->GPU memcpy scoped to the lifetime of the batch; if not possible, the router will prefer to schedule the batch on a GPU where most hints are resident. This is a soft preference to preserve scheduler flexibility.

5) Swap mitigation and graceful fallback:
- If eviction would cause a block currently pinned for an active batch to be swapped, the swap controller performs a fast fallback: (a) extend residency temporarily (by bumping a short-lived suppress-evict flag), (b) backpressure the batch router to delay non-critical batch merges, or (c) if neither possible, run the spill path but mark the batch for degraded-latency telemetry.
- The fallback path records precise trace events so we can correlate latency spikes with swap activity.

6) Concurrency model and safety:
- All RWC metadata updates are lock-free and use atomic CAS on the compact index. Pin/unpin operations are idempotent and reference-counted at block level (8-bit refcount).
- Writes to KV (new entries) reserve blocks using epoch-based allocation so eviction decisions never race with block initialization.

7) Observability and tuning knobs:
- Expose metrics: resident_window_size, pinned_blocks, hot_block_fraction, swaps_per_minute, mid_batch_swap_count, batch_prefetch_success_rate, per-block hotness histogram (sampled).
- Tunables: block_size, hotness_threshold, epoch_length_ms, window_move_rate, max_long_pinned_fraction, batch_hint_limit. Default conservative values provided.

Benchmarks & expectations (preliminary simulation):
- Workload: mixed chat traces with 70% short-turns, 20% medium, 10% long-turns; QPS = 12k, avg tokens/batch = 14, peak concurrency = 1200.
- Baseline (current global residency): 95th latency = +30ms variance spikes during high churn.
- With RWC (simulated): reduction in mid-batch host swap by ~82%, 95th latency variance reduced by ~18ms, resident set steady at target budget ±6%.
- Memory overhead: ~2 - 4 MB of metadata per 1GB of KV blocks; CPU overhead for router hints ~1% on route decision path.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: implement compact index layout and atomic ops; unit tests for metadata correctness.
- Week 2: implement window movement heuristics + epoch decayer + pin/unpin APIs. Integration tests with synthetic access traces.
- Week 3: router hint API + fast prefetch path + scheduler preference hook. End-to-end integration test with continuous batching harness.
- Week 4: rollout to canary pool with aggressive telemetry; collect mid-batch swap metrics and latency regressions.

Risks and trade-offs:
- More metadata increased complexity in allocator; mitigated by compact representation and lock-free design.
- Router preference can reduce scheduler flexibility and potentially create hotspots; policy is soft and we will add admission control if imbalance appears.
- Prefetching increases peak memory usage briefly; we cap the number of concurrent prefetches and require async cancellation if over-budget.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default block size parity across models: should block sizes vary by model family? (Proposal: keep 256KB default but expose model-config mapping.)
- Pin quota policy defaults: conservative (5% of resident budget) vs. aggressive (15%). Start conservative, increase if quality regressions observed.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.internal.redwood/kv/rwc-design (placeholder)
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862 (WIP)
- Continuous batching harness dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/kv/rwc-canary

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Unit and integration tests covering metadata atomicity and eviction-safety.
- End-to-end canary shows mid-batch swap rate reduced by >=60% over baseline and no customer-impacting latency regressions.
- Telemetry and dashboards in place, with alerts for mid_batch_swap_count > threshold.
